_README: Repairs for the DOUBLED-consonant corruption class: a consonant emitted
twice with no intervening halant (ययह -> यह, सहाययता -> सहायता). This is
a different class from data/conjunct_repairs.json, which repairs DROPPED
consonants (ग्ाम -> ग्राम); the two maps share no entries.
textnorm.normalize() deliberately does not collapse a doubled consonant
that is followed by another consonant, because a blanket rule corrupts
real words (ममता -> मता). normalize_header() may be aggressive because a
header is only ever used for segmentation, never quoted to a parent.
That left body prose unrepaired in 32% of in-syllabus chunks.
A word-level map is the safe middle path: it can only ever change a token
listed here, so a word not in the map cannot be corrupted. Candidates were
generated by requiring the collapsed form to be MORE frequent in the
corpus than the doubled one, then hand-audited — see _REJECTED, which is
why the frequency test alone is not enough.
Regenerate candidates with: scripts/find_doubled_consonants.py
'restores' is the opposite direction and a separate finding: real words that
textnorm's own _DUP_AFTER_HALANT rule collapses. That rule asserts a
consonant doubled after a halant 'is always an artifact', which is false for
अध्ययन (ध्य + यन) — it becomes अध्यन, and 35 of the corpus's 41 spellings were
already the broken form. Restoring is unambiguous because अध्यन is not a Hindi
word, so the rule is narrowed by exact match rather than by loosening a regex
that the 0.7% CER measurement was tuned against.

_REJECTED.अध्ययन: अध्ययन is a real Hindi word whose य-य is legitimate. Frequency approved अध्ययन -> अध्यन because अध्यन occurs 35 times against अध्ययन's 6 — but अध्यन is itself a corruption, of the DROPPED consonant class. Repairing here would have turned the only correct spellings in the corpus into the common corruption. This is the ममता hazard textnorm.normalize_header() documents, reached by a different road.
